title: Seagrass
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Seagrass”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: Seagrasses are the only embryophytes (commonly referred to as "land plants") which grow in marine environments. There are about 60 species of fully marine seagrasses which belong to four families (Posidoniaceae, Zosteraceae, Hydrocharitaceae and Cymodoceaceae), all in the order Alismatales (in the clade of monocotyledons). Seagrasses evolved from terrestrial plants which recolonised the ocean 70 to 100 million years ago.

The name seagrass stems from the many species with long and narrow leaves, which grow by rhizome extension and often spread across large "meadows" resembling grassland; many species superficially resemble terrestrial grasses of the family Poaceae.

Like all autotrophic plants, seagrasses photosynthesize, in the submerged photic zone, and most occur in shallow and sheltered coastal waters anchored in sand or mud bottoms. Most species undergo submarine pollination and complete their life cycle underwater. While it was previously believed this pollination was carried out without pollinators and purely by sea current drift, this has been shown to be false for at least one species, Thalassia testudinum, which carries out a mixed biotic-abiotic strategy. Crustaceans (such as crabs, Majidae zoae, Thalassinidea zoea) and syllid polychaete worm larvae have both been found with pollen grains, the plant producing nutritious mucigenous clumps of pollen to attract and stick to them instead of nectar as terrestrial flowers do.

Seagrasses form dense underwater seagrass meadows which are among the most productive ecosystems in the world. They function as important carbon sinks and provide habitats and food for a diversity of marine life comparable to that of coral reefs.

sentence.text: Seagrasses form dense underwater seagrass meadows which are among the most productive ecosystems in the world.
sentence.translation: 海草形成茂密的水下海草床，这些海草床属于世界上生产力最高的生态系统之列。
sentence.analysis: 主句主干是 Seagrasses form ... meadows，form 是谓语动词，表示“形成”。dense 和 underwater 都修饰 seagrass meadows，分别说明茂密程度和所在环境。which 引导定语从句，先行词是 seagrass meadows，which 在从句中作主语。be among the most productive ecosystems 表示“属于生产力最高的生态系统之列”，不是说海草床是唯一生产力最高的生态系统。in the world 限定比较范围。

questions.prompt: 第三段关于 Thalassia testudinum 的发现如何改变了此前对海草传粉的认识？
options: 它说明海草不能进行光合作用
它证明海流不参与任何海草的传粉
它表明至少一种海草的传粉并非完全不需要动物参与
它说明所有海草都必须离开水体才能传粉
questions.explanation: 第三段说，以前认为海草传粉完全依靠海流且没有传粉者，但这至少对 Thalassia testudinum 不成立。文中接着提到带有花粉的甲壳类和蠕虫幼体，支持生物参与传粉的解释；结论不能扩大为所有海草都采用同一种策略。
hints: 只推出原文足以支持的结论，警惕扩大范围。

questions.prompt: 根据最后一段，下列哪组作用都属于海草床的生态作用？
options: 让海洋生物不再需要食物，并阻止所有海流
仅为一种鱼类提供食物，并减少所有水下植被
将珊瑚礁变成陆地，并为陆生动物提供草原
储存碳，并为多种海洋生物提供栖息地和食物
questions.explanation: 最后一段指出海草床是 important carbon sinks，并且 provide habitats and food for a diversity of marine life。这里比较的是海洋生物的多样性，并没有说海草床会把珊瑚礁转变为其他地形。
